texts: Three months after CABG, an ejection fraction still at 28% despite a good recovery is an indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.
An ICD for primary prevention is advised when the ejection fraction stays at 35% or less in NYHA class II or III, at least 90 days after revascularisation and 40 days after an infarction.
The waiting period lets stunned or hibernating muscle recover; his ejection fraction rose only from 22% to 28%, so he remains at high risk of sudden death.
Feeling well does not lower that risk, and Holter monitoring or another echo only delays protection.
An LVAD is for advanced heart failure, not for a man in class II.
In the picture, the bodyguard seizes Pinocchio before he strikes, while the reaper waits beside the open coffin and the hourglass is empty.
Memory hook: an empty hourglass and a weak bouncer: hire the bodyguard.
